name: Immutable Group Member Index

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Immutable Group Member Index Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

Each immutable group snapshot walks the whole source order and filters by group key (O(n) hash lookups), and a regrouping batch takes at least four snapshots, so one regroup in a 10k-row cache with 16 groups costs ~50 µs although each group holds ~625 rows. Keeping each group's member keys in source order (inserted by binary search on source positions, repositioned when a key moves, removed on regroup/removal) lets a snapshot read only its members: O(group) instead of O(n). A debug assertion compares every indexed snapshot with the full scan.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** per-group member index in source order for cache immutable group snapshots.
**Allowed changes:** `ImmutableCacheGroupState` (struct in `immutable_cache_group_entry.rs`, impl in `ungrouped_cache_state.rs`).
**Forbidden in this experiment:** list immutable groups, live groups, snapshot diffing/move logic.

Focused tests: `collections::tests::{group_and_combiner_indexes,grouping_tree_switching,snapshot_diff_indexes,index_contract_harness,ordered_emission_core,operator_input_interop}` and public API tests (debug assertion compares with the scan); clippy/fmt. Bench `operator_updates` (group-immutable). Pass: group-immutable update >=3x faster.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

group-immutable regrouping update from ~50 us to ~10-15 us (four O(group) snapshots remain inherent).
